scope: Bounded parallelism for the final transitive dependency graph revalidation phase. No cache, reduced coverage, worker-limit increase or board geometry change.
implementation: Extract the existing input-ordered bounded work queue into an internal helper and use it for both complete translation-unit scans and final graph revalidation. The phases do not overlap or nest. Every launched task is joined; earliest manifest-index failure wins; successful census merge remains manifest ordered. One retained AST projection remains the limit.

tests.new_adversarial_cases: All worker limits 1..4: exactly-once disjoint results, active-worker bound and completed joins, empty phase. Limits 2..4: explicitly ordered fast later failure and delayed earlier failure must report earlier failure after joining. Invalid worker counts reject. Existing real-compiler serial/parallel parity and concurrent dependency mutation tests remain active.

compiler_wave_regression.description: Final -M compiler requests rendezvous after their respective macro passes, proving actual final-phase concurrency for configured worker limits 2, 3 and 4. This test fails if final graph discovery is accidentally serialized.

measurement.status: Full workload completed successfully with exact census parity and lower observed wall time in one sequential pair.
measurement.protocol: Sequential full 69-file scans using the same source manifest, flags, compiler and two-worker cap. Compile/test work occurs between, not during, measured scans. OS caches uncontrolled; limited repetition. Source audit time only, not board generation, rendering, compile time or a historical Python comparison.

limitations: Dependency consistency remains observation-based, not an atomic filesystem snapshot or sufficient persistent cache key. No full-board qualification or smaller-layout claim. Other sustained goal requirements remain open.
